COOK – FULL TIME

BUSINESS:  PAPADOPOULOS BROTHERS PTY LTD
ABN: 68 607 569 380
TRADING AS: Meli Annandale
LOCATION: 88 View Street, Annandale NSW 2038
SALARY: $79,500 – $83,000 + Superannuation (commensurate with experience)
EMPLOYMENT TYPE: Full-time (minimum 38 hours per week)

Job Published: 3 July 2026


ABOUT THE BUSINESS
Meli Annandale is a contemporary neighbourhood café located in Annandale, NSW, providing high-quality breakfast, brunch, and lunch dining within a modern hospitality environment. The café offers a diverse menu featuring freshly prepared contemporary Australian café cuisine, specialty coffee, and seasonal menu offerings, with a strong focus on quality ingredients, presentation, and customer experience.
The business operates a full-service dine-in model with prepared-to-order meals delivered across continuous daily service. Kitchen operations involve fresh ingredient preparation, coordinated food production, and efficient workflow management to meet varying customer demand, particularly during peak breakfast, brunch, and weekend trading periods.
The commercial kitchen operates under established systems and procedures, incorporating food preparation, cooking, plating, stock management, and strict compliance with Australian food safety, hygiene, and workplace health and safety standards to ensure consistent service quality and operational efficiency.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The position of Cook is a hands-on operational role responsible for preparing, cooking, and presenting menu items in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and service requirements within a contemporary café environment. The role requires the ability to manage allocated kitchen sections, maintain consistency across breakfast, brunch, and lunch service, and contribute to the efficient day-to-day operation of a commercial kitchen.
The successful candidate will work collaboratively within a team-based environment, demonstrating initiative in food preparation, coordinating workflow during service, maintaining food quality and presentation standards, and ensuring compliance with food safety and hygiene requirements.
The primary place of employment will be Meli Annandale, 88 View Street, Annandale NSW 2038. From time to time, the successful candidate may also be required to perform duties at the employer's associated hospitality venue, Sabine Bondi, Shop 505/500 Oxford Street, Bondi Junction NSW 2022, to support operational requirements. Duties performed at either location will remain consistent with the position of Cook and will be undertaken under the direction of the employer.
The role also provides ongoing opportunities for professional development through structured on-the-job training and exposure to a range of contemporary café kitchen operations and cooking techniques.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

FOOD PREPARATION AND COOKING
•	Prepare, cook, and present a range of breakfast, brunch, and lunch menu items in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and presentation requirements.
•	Undertake ingredient preparation, including washing, cutting, portioning, marinating, and pre-service mise en place to support efficient kitchen operations.
•	Apply appropriate cooking techniques including grilling, frying, roasting, baking, poaching, and sautéing while maintaining consistency in quality and presentation.
•	Follow standardised recipes and portion controls to ensure consistency, minimise wastage, and meet service expectations.
•	Adjust food preparation and cooking methods where required to accommodate service volumes, dietary requirements, and special customer requests.

SERVICE AND KITCHEN OPERATIONS
•	Support efficient kitchen workflow during breakfast, brunch, and lunch service to ensure timely preparation and delivery of meals.
•	Manage allocated kitchen sections, ensuring workstations are organised and service-ready prior to and during operational periods.
•	Communicate effectively with kitchen and front-of-house staff to support efficient service delivery and order accuracy.
•	Assist with menu execution, daily specials, and seasonal menu offerings in accordance with business requirements.
•	Adapt workflow during busy service periods while maintaining food quality, presentation, and operational efficiency.

STOCK CONTROL AND KITCHEN ORGANISATION
•	Assist in receiving, inspecting, and storing deliveries to ensure product quality and compliance with storage requirements.
•	Implement stock rotation practices, including FIFO, to maintain freshness and minimise wastage.
•	Monitor ingredient usage and report stock shortages or inconsistencies to senior kitchen staff.
•	Assist with stocktakes and maintain organised storage areas to support efficient kitchen operations.
•	Ensure appropriate labelling, storage, and handling of food products in accordance with food safety standards.

FOOD SAFETY AND COMPLIANCE
•	Maintain compliance with food safety legislation and safe food handling procedures.
•	Maintain high standards of hygiene and cleanliness across workstations, equipment, utensils, and food preparation areas.
•	Monitor storage, cooking, and holding temperatures to ensure compliance with food safety requirements.
•	Follow workplace food safety procedures, including HACCP-based practices where applicable.
•	Comply with Workplace Health and Safety requirements, including the safe operation of commercial kitchen equipment.

GENERAL DUTIES AND TEAM CONTRIBUTION
•	Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient workstation throughout each shift.
•	Follow instructions from senior kitchen staff and management with accuracy and attention to detail.
•	Work collaboratively within a team environment to support efficient kitchen operations during busy service periods.
•	Demonstrate reliability, professionalism, punctuality, and a positive approach to work.
•	Participate in ongoing training and professional development to enhance culinary skills and operational performance.

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS
•	Relevant qualification in Commercial Cookery (Certificate III or higher) or a closely related field, or a minimum of one (1) year of relevant experience within a commercial kitchen environment.
•	Demonstrated experience preparing and cooking food within a commercial café, restaurant, or hospitality environment.
•	Sound knowledge of food safety standards, kitchen hygiene, and safe food handling practices.
•	Ability to work efficiently within a fast-paced commercial kitchen environment.
•	Availability to work weekends, public holidays, and varied rostered shifts as required.

KEY COMPETENCIES
•	Technical Cooking Proficiency
•	Contemporary Café Food Preparation
•	Recipe Interpretation & Food Presentation
•	Time Management
•	Kitchen Workflow & Operational Awareness
•	Attention to Detail
•	Communication & Team Collaboration
•	Problem Solving
•	Food Safety & Compliance
•	Commitment to Continuous Improvement

HOW TO APPLY
Please submit a one-page CV outlining your relevant experience, qualifications, and availability. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted

Employment Type: Full-time (minimum 38 hours per week)
Job Published: 6 July 2026

ABOUT THE BUSINESS
Oliver Street Kitchen is a contemporary restaurant located in Heathcote, New South Wales, offering a modern dining experience centred on quality food, fresh ingredients, and professional customer service. The restaurant operates lunch and dinner services and provides a diverse menu featuring contemporary Australian cuisine complemented by selected international influences, with a strong emphasis on freshly prepared meals, premium ingredients, and consistent food quality.
The commercial kitchen prepares a broad range of freshly cooked dishes including premium meat, poultry, seafood, pasta, salad, and seasonal menu offerings. Kitchen operations involve coordinated food preparation, commercial cooking, stock management, quality control, and efficient service delivery to meet varying customer demand during lunch, dinner, weekends, and peak trading periods.
Oliver Street Kitchen is committed to maintaining high culinary standards through established kitchen procedures, continuous quality improvement, and strict compliance with Australian food safety, hygiene, and Workplace Health and Safety requirements.

ABOUT THE ROLE
Oliver Street Kitchen has an opportunity available for an experienced Cook to join its kitchen team on a full-time basis.
This is a hands-on operational role responsible for preparing, cooking, and presenting a broad range of contemporary Australian and internationally inspired dishes in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and service requirements. The successful candidate will contribute to all aspects of kitchen operations, including food preparation, cooking, plating, stock control, and maintaining a safe and efficient commercial kitchen environment.
The role requires the ability to manage allocated kitchen sections, coordinate workflow during busy lunch and dinner service periods, maintain consistency in food quality and presentation, and work collaboratively with kitchen and front-of-house staff to ensure efficient service delivery and a high standard of customer satisfaction.
This is a full-time permanent position based on a minimum 38-hour working week.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Food Preparation and Cooking
• Prepare, cook, and present a wide range of contemporary Australian and internationally inspired dishes in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and presentation requirements.
• Prepare premium meat, poultry, seafood, pasta, salad, and seasonal menu items using appropriate commercial cooking techniques including grilling, roasting, frying, baking, poaching, braising, and sautéing.
• Undertake ingredient preparation including washing, cutting, trimming, portioning, marinating, and mise en place to support efficient kitchen operations.
• Monitor cooking times, temperatures, seasoning, and presentation to ensure consistency and quality across all dishes.
• Adjust food preparation and cooking methods where required to accommodate service demands, dietary requirements, and customer requests.

Kitchen Operations and Service Delivery
• Support efficient kitchen workflow during lunch and dinner service to ensure timely preparation and delivery of meals.
• Manage allocated kitchen sections, ensuring workstations remain organised, clean, and service-ready throughout each shift.
• Communicate effectively with kitchen and front-of-house staff to support coordinated service delivery and order accuracy.
• Assist with the preparation and execution of daily specials and seasonal menu offerings.
• Adapt efficiently to changing service demands while maintaining food quality, presentation, and operational efficiency.

Stock Control and Kitchen Organisation
• Assist with receiving, inspecting, storing, and rotating food supplies in accordance with established stock control procedures.
• Apply FIFO stock rotation principles to minimise spoilage and maintain product freshness.
• Monitor stock usage and advise senior kitchen staff of inventory shortages or ordering requirements.
• Participate in stocktakes and maintain organised storage areas to support efficient kitchen operations.
• Ensure appropriate labelling, storage, and handling of food products in accordance with food safety requirements.

Food Safety and Compliance
• Maintain compliance with Australian Food Safety Standards and safe food handling practices.
• Maintain high standards of hygiene and cleanliness throughout food preparation areas, equipment, utensils, and workstations.
• Monitor food storage, preparation, cooking, cooling, and holding temperatures to ensure regulatory compliance.
• Follow workplace food safety procedures and cleaning schedules to maintain a safe commercial kitchen environment.
• Comply with Workplace Health and Safety requirements, including the safe operation and maintenance of commercial kitchen equipment.

General Duties and Team Contribution
• Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient workstation throughout each shift.
• Work collaboratively with kitchen staff and management to support efficient daily operations.
• Demonstrate reliability, professionalism, punctuality, and a positive team-oriented approach.
• Follow instructions from senior kitchen staff with accuracy and attention to detail.
• Participate in ongoing workplace training and continuous professional development to further culinary skills and operational knowledge.

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS
• Relevant qualification in Commercial Cookery (Certificate III or higher) or a closely related field, together with at least one (1) year of relevant full-time experience in a commercial kitchen; or equivalent skills and experience suitable for the position.
• Demonstrated experience preparing and cooking meals within a commercial restaurant, hospitality, or food service environment.
• Sound knowledge of Australian Food Safety Standards, kitchen hygiene, and safe food handling practices.
• Ability to prepare and cook a diverse range of contemporary Australian cuisine using a variety of commercial cooking techniques.
• Experience working efficiently within a fast-paced commercial kitchen environment.
• Availability to work weekends, evenings, public holidays, and rostered shifts as required.

KEY COMPETENCIES
• Technical commercial cookery skills.
• Contemporary Australian cuisine preparation.
• Food preparation, cooking, and presentation.
• Time management and organisational skills.
• Kitchen workflow and service coordination.
• Attention to detail and quality control.
• Communication and teamwork.
• Problem-solving and adaptability.
• Food safety and regulatory compliance.
• Commitment to continuous improvement and professional standards.

HOW TO APPLY
Please submit a one-page CV outlining your relevant qualifications, experience, and availability.
Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

The AMA Group, is Australia's largest network of accident repair facilities, which currently comprises of over 120 outlets and over 2,200 employees across Australia and New Zealand.

The AMA Group's success is a result of our commitment of providing our clients and work providers with quality and cost-effective repairs, as well as exceptional customer service. Our people is what makes this possible and are therefore our focus. We invest in our people. Creating the leaders of today and developing the skills for tomorrow.

 

About Capital S.M.A.R.T

With over 50 repair centres across Australia and New Zealand, Capital S.M.A.R.T Repairs is the industry leader of the collision repair industry, specialising in small, medium, and larger repairs. We are the pioneers of customer satisfaction and innovation standards, and pride ourselves on providing our employees with safe, supportive, and rewarding working conditions.

About the Role

We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced and qualified Insurance Loss Adjustor to join either our AMA Group Solutions or Capital S.M.A.R.T Repairs team to undertake quality workmanship to ensure vehicles are returned to their pre-accident condition. This is a full-time position located in all areas of Regional NSW.

The primary purpose of this role is to be responsible for the timely completion of accurate and comprehensive quotes for accident repairs on vehicles. You will apply your knowledge of motor vehicles and your skills with computers whilst interacting with a range of people. 

Reporting to the Centre Manager this role will work within our large network of repair facilities and you will be provided with stability and opportunity.

Key Responsibilities:
- Providing excellent customer service to clients and work providers
- Accurately quote vehicles in a timely manner and in accordance with average repair cost targets and insurer/company procedures
- Complete quotes as required onsite, off-site and online
- Processing vehicles onsite by carrying out vehicle arrival inspections, including mapping and imaging

- Manage suppliers to ensure additional work is recorded and authorised in a timely manner
- Assist with production management of the centre where required
- Ensure vehicles are repaired to their pre-accident condition
- Hand over completed repairs to customers

- Proven experience within a similar position including experience in the preparation of estimates / quotations in the automotive smash repair industry

- Excellent customer service skills including building rapport with customers and work providers
- Highly professional and personable
- Strong systems experience and competent computer abilities
- Excel an advantage but not a necessary

- Ability to meet strict deadlines
- Ability to problem solve and excellent accuracy and attention to detail
- Able to work effectively and collaboratively with the team
- Strong commitment to work in a safe manner
- High attention to detail
- Be reliable, punctual & hardworking

We are leaders in the repair industry and offer
-Team environment
-Ongoing training
-Career opportunity
-Latest tools, equipment and process
-Great opportunity to earn big $$$ for competent and efficient tradespeople
-Junior-Mid experienced tradesperson $60-$80k
-Mid-Senior tradesperson $80k-$100k
-Annual salary

Relevate is a Brisbane-based operations, strategy and technology consulting firm that helps businesses unlock the full value of their software. We work across CRM implementation, IT managed services, virtual staffing and digital transformation advisory, with particular depth in the Zoho ecosystem. Plenty of firms can install software; our real point of difference is adoption. We make sure the people using the tools genuinely embrace them, because that is where return on investment is actually realised. Our work is practical and outcome-driven. We have helped clients cut integration costs, reduce monthly licensing spend and reclaim days of manual reporting time each month simply by rethinking how their systems fit together. In short, we help teams work smarter rather than harder, so our clients become more profitable, more valuable and more resilient.

ICT Customer Support Officer | Relevate — Brisbane, QLD

Key Responsibilities
•	Serve as a first point of contact for clients experiencing issues with their CRM, business applications or supporting hardware, diagnosing problems and delivering timely resolutions
•	Assess client needs and recommend suitable software, hardware and system configurations to resolve operational challenges and close value gaps in their business tools
•	Customise and adapt existing applications, including Zoho Creator apps, CRM workflows and automations, so they align with each client's specific processes
•	Install, configure and deploy Zoho modules and other business software across client environments, ensuring each solution is set up correctly for the way the client works
•	Support and drive effective adoption of implemented systems by training end users and monitoring usage, so applications and equipment are used efficiently and deliver maximum value
•	Assist with implementing client networks and integrations between platforms, including connecting systems through tools such as Zoho Flow, and support the build and ongoing upkeep of client web portals and websites
•	Troubleshoot, repair or arrange replacement of peripheral equipment such as printers, modems and workstations as part of our managed services support
•	Assemble, install, maintain and repair computer hardware, software and related equipment as required, keeping client systems reliable with minimal disruption
•	Log, track and prioritise support requests, maintaining accurate records of issues and resolutions
•	Document configurations, fixes and processes to build and maintain an internal knowledge base
•	Escalate complex or unresolved matters to senior consultants and collaborate with the wider team to deliver solutions
•	Provide both remote and on-site support to clients as needed, and assist virtual staffing team members with the tools and systems they rely on

Skills, Qualifications and Experience
•	An AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in a relevant field
•	At least 1 year of experience in an ICT support or similar customer-facing technical role

Personal Attributes
•	Genuinely customer-focused, with a patient and approachable manner
•	Well organised, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines
•	Comfortable working both independently and as part of a close-knit team
•	Keen to keep learning and to stay across new technologies and platforms

Hours and Remuneration
This is a full-time position of approximately 38 hours per week. We are offering a salary of $75,000 to $85,000 plus superannuation per annum for the successful applicant.

If you enjoy solving problems, helping people and working with modern business technology, we would love to hear from you.

They now seek a skilled and qualified Telecommunication Lines Worker to join their team in Lutana in TAS on a full time basis.

This is for a full time position with an annual salary between $80,000 to $85,000 depending on experience plus superannuation. The role will be based in Lutana in TAS.

Reviewing blueprints, schematics, and specifications for equipment installations and understanding where and how the equipment (loopaline, jdsu linester, fiber meter, pon meter, lockout kit, gas detector, video probe, harnsess & ladders) will be positioned and connected to ensure correct installation and functionality. 

Using various instruments such as ohmmeters, voltmeters, ammeters, and transmission measuring equipment to detect faults or malfunctions in telecommunications systems. This involves diagnosing issues in wiring, equipment, or signal transmission. 

Connecting wiring and cables to different appliances or equipment. This involves proper handling of wires to ensure secure and safe connections for functionality. 

Adjusting, replacing, or repairing the faulty components. Also, testing the equipment using electronic instruments to ensure it functions correctly. 

Installing various types of cabling systems for telecommunications, including those used for telephones, radio broadcasts, pay TV, and internet transmission. This involves both physical installation and ensuring proper signal flow. This involves connecting cables together securely and sealing the cable sheaths using lead or thermoplastic materials to ensure the integrity of the connection, especially in outdoor or harsh environments. 

Installing, maintaining, and troubleshooting both aerial (above-ground) and underground wiring systems for various telecommunications services. This includes erecting antennas for radio and mobile phone communication and ensuring they perform optimal 

Installing telecommunication devices like telephones, switchboards, and data transmission equipment and ensures these devices are set up correctly and are functioning according to specifications. 

 

 

The Requirements: 

At least a Diploma qualification in Telecommunications or a related field 

At least 2 years full time post qualification experience as a Telecommunications Lines Worker  

At least 2 years’ experience installing, maintaining, testing, and fault finding telecommunications copper, fibre, aerial, underground, and customer premises cabling systems 

At least 2 years’ experience using telecommunications testing equipment including Loopaline, JDSU line tester, fibre meter, PON meter, ohmmeters, voltmeters, ammeters, and transmission measuring instruments 

At least 2 years’ experience diagnosing signal loss, cable faults, wiring defects, equipment malfunction, poor transmission quality, and connectivity failures across telecommunications networks 

At least 2 years’ experience terminating, jointing, sealing, repairing, and securing telecommunications cables, including lead or thermoplastic sheath sealing for outdoor and underground cable integrity 

At least 2 years’ experience installing and commissioning telecommunication devices, antennas, switchboards, data transmission equipment, internet cabling, pay TV cabling, and telephone systems 

Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to perform on-site analysis and resolution of technical problems 

Ability to work independently and as part of a team 

Familiarity with maintaining detailed logs and documentation of inventories, parts, equipment, and instruments, as well as communication policies and procedures 

Ability to liaise effectively with vendors, suppliers, service providers, and external resources to monitor contractual obligations and performance delivery

For the Love of Food! Join the Sodexo team
Do you want to be part of one of the country’s largest and most diverse Chef Teams?

Sodexo inspires and nurtures our chefs to become leaders in their industry and deliver fantastic food which delights our customers. All we ask is that you have a passion for what you do and an eye for innovation.
